items.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: because he had respect for Igor Stravinsky

ctx.x: And you’d go in and record the tunes, and then the fellow that played him had to match up to, or try to.

Yeah, the best, you know, pantomime. A lot of things they were able to retrieve and use from Charlie Parker. Some things they were not able to do either because of the technology of it, or because of contractual situations like money or whatever. And in those instances I was involved. And then there were incidental scenes during the movie where certain background things needed to be, and of course Bird’s not there, and well they didn’t use him for things like that. There was one scene in the movie involving…
Was there any attempt to figure out, well, what key is his piece in?
